source_metadata.question_text: Let <math><mi>p</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo></math> be a polynomial of degree <math><mn>5</mn></math> such that <math><mi>p</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>n</mi><mrow><msup><mi>n</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></math> for <math><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math>, <math><mn>3</mn></math>, <math><mn>4</mn></math>, <math><mn>5</mn></math>, <math><mn>6</mn></math>, <math><mn>7</mn></math>. Find <math><mi>p</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>)</mo></math>.
source_metadata.explanation: Define <math><mi>q</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msup><mi>x</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></math>. Then <math><mi>q</mi></math> has degree <math><mn>7</mn></math> and zeros at <math><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></math> to <math><mn>7</mn></math>, so <math><mi>q</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mo>−</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mn>29</mn><mi>x</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>27</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>⋯</mo><mo>(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>7</mn><mo>)</mo></mrow></mfrac><mn>40320</mn></math> using the conditions <math><mi>q</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></math> and <math><mi>q</mi><mo>(</mo><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>. Evaluating gives <math><mi>q</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mn>37</mn><mn>8</mn></mfrac></math>, so <math><mi>p</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>8</mn><mo>)</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><mrow><msup><mn>8</mn><mn>2</mn></msup><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>56</mn></mfrac></math>.

derived_analysis.sub_skill: Using auxiliary polynomials and root-factorization to determine coefficients
derived_analysis.problem_family: Find the value of a polynomial at a new point given its values at several integers by constructing an auxiliary polynomial with prescribed roots
solve_strategy: Introduce q(x) = (x^2 - 1) p(x) - x so that q(n)=0 for the given integer inputs n because (n^2-1)p(n)-n = 0.
Recognize deg q = deg p + 2, so q is degree 7 and thus equals (ax + b) * P(x), where P(x) = ∏_{k=2}^7 (x - k).
Use evaluations at x=1 and x=-1 to produce two linear equations for a and b (these points annihilate the (x^2-1) factor so q(±1) give small integers).
Solve the 2×2 linear system for a and b, compute P(8) and evaluate q(8) = (a*8 + b)*P(8).
Recover p(8) from p(8) = (q(8) + 8)/(8^2 - 1) and reduce the resulting fraction.
derived_analysis.reasoning_pattern: Transform the problem by multiplying by a factor that cancels the denominator at known inputs to create a polynomial with known integer roots, then determine its missing linear factor via evaluations at special points.
logic_invariants: For each given integer n in {2,3,4,5,6,7}, q(n) = (n^2 - 1)p(n) - n = 0.
q(x) is divisible by P(x) = ∏_{k=2}^7 (x - k); therefore q(x) = (ax + b)P(x).
Evaluations at x = 1 and x = -1 eliminate the (x^2 - 1) factor so q(±1) equal -1 and +1 respectively, giving linear constraints on a and b independent of p(±1).
P(8) = 6! = 720 is used to scale q(8) and relates to factorial-like products of consecutive integers.
changeable_parameters: list_of_integer_points_where_values_known (start and length, consecutive or nonconsecutive)
value_formula_at_these_points (e.g., n/(n^2 - 1), linear in n, other rational forms)
auxiliary_factor_used (e.g., x^2 - 1 or x^2 - a) that clears denominators
target_evaluation_point (the x at which p(x) is requested)
parameter_constraints: Number of independent conditions provided must be consistent with deg p (to avoid under- or over-determined systems); with deg p = d, providing d+1 independent values determines p uniquely.

The auxiliary factor chosen should cancel denominators at the provided inputs (i.e., its zeros should match any n that make denominators zero) or be chosen so cancellations produce integer/known q(±1) values.
When representing q(x) = (ax + b)P(x), P(x) must have degree equal to the number of distinct known roots; to make q one degree higher, multiply P by a linear factor (ax + b).
Avoid selecting known input values that make denominator zero unless the construction explicitly handles the resulting indeterminate p(n).
derived_analysis.answer_format: Multiple-choice letter plus numeric content as a reduced rational fraction (e.g., 3/56).
rendering_notes: Preserve MathML tags exactly when rendering: all <math>...</math> and embedded <mi>, <mo>, <mn>, <mfrac>, <msup>, etc. must be kept.

generation_knobs: vary degree_of_p; vary consecutive integer range (length and start); vary numerator/denominator form (e.g., n/(n^2 - k), an+b over polynomial); change auxiliary factor (x^2 - 1 -> x^2 - c); change target evaluation point (8 -> other integer).

safe_variations: change the consecutive integer block while adjusting degree accordingly; replace n/(n^2-1) with other rational forms that are cleared by a simple auxiliary factor; ask for p at a different integer not among provided points.

unsafe_variations: include provided n that make denominators zero without adjusting construction (introduces undefined p(n) unless handled); pick value_formula that does not lead to a polynomial p of the specified degree; choose nonconsecutive points without providing enough conditions to determine the polynomial.

novelty_opportunities: use auxiliary factors of higher degree (e.g., (x^2 - a)(x - b)) to craft problems with multi-parameter linear factors; ask for coefficients of p rather than a single value; ask for p at a point inside the given set to test handling of removable singularities.

validation_rules: ensure the number of provided constraints matches degree+1 (or explicitly state additional structure to make the polynomial unique); verify that auxiliary factor zeros and provided input set are consistent; check arithmetic simplifications (factorials and cancellations) and fraction reduction.
risk_flags: Misinterpreting p(1) or p(-1): although p(±1) may be undefined because denominator zero, q(±1) are still well-defined and provide constraints.
Arithmetic errors in computing large products like P(1) or P(-1) (factorials) and sign mistakes when evaluating products of negatives.
For generated variants, accidentally producing an underdetermined or overdetermined system if the relationship between degree and number of points is not preserved.
Failing to reduce rational answers to lowest terms or mismatching the multiple-choice letter with the computed numeric value.

changeable_parameters.name: degree_of_p
constraints: typically between 3 and 7 for manageable arithmetic

changeable_parameters.name: known_points_start
changeable_parameters.role: start of a consecutive integer block used as known inputs (first n)
constraints: choose so that auxiliary_factor zeros are not inside the block unless intended
block will be known_points_start .. known_points_start + known_points_count - 1

changeable_parameters.name: known_points_count
changeable_parameters.role: number of consecutive known integer inputs
constraints: must equal degree_of_p + 1 unless additional structure is provided

changeable_parameters.name: value_formula_template
changeable_parameters.role: formula for p(n) at known integer inputs (use n as placeholder)
changeable_parameters.suggested_range: rational expressions in n that can be cleared by a low-degree auxiliary factor
constraints: should evaluate to a rational number for each known point
denominators should be cancelable by the chosen auxiliary_factor

changeable_parameters.name: auxiliary_factor
changeable_parameters.role: polynomial factor multiplied by p(x) to clear denominators and create integer roots
changeable_parameters.suggested_range: low-degree polynomials like x^2 - c, x - c, (x^2 - c)(x - d)
constraints: must vanish at any known point where value_formula denominator is zero
degree should be small (1 or 2) for solvable linear-factor cases

changeable_parameters.name: target_evaluation_point
changeable_parameters.role: the x-value where p(x) is requested
changeable_parameters.suggested_range: an integer not in known_points (but can be adjacent)
constraints: preferably not one of the known_points
chosen so that target^2 - c (denominator of recovery formula) is nonzero

generation_guidance: must_change: For each generated instance change at least one of {degree_of_p, known_points_start, value_formula_template, auxiliary_factor, target_evaluation_point} so the new instance is materially different.
allowed_variations: vary degree_of_p within suggested_range and set known_points_count = degree_of_p + 1; shift the consecutive block (known_points_start) and recompute P(x) accordingly.
allowed_variations: replace value_formula_template with other rational forms like (an + b)/(n^2 - c) provided auxiliary_factor is updated to cancel denominators.
allowed_variations: change auxiliary_factor to a different low-degree polynomial that cancels denominators at known points (e.g., x^2 - c or (x - c)(x - d)).
forbidden_variations: do not choose known_points_count different from degree_of_p + 1 unless extra constraints are explicitly provided (would under/overdetermine the polynomial).
forbidden_variations: do not include known points that make denominators zero unless auxiliary_factor includes those zeros to cancel them.

instance_acceptance_rules: validate that number_of_known_points == degree_of_p + 1 (unless the generator includes extra structure); validate that auxiliary_factor zeros include any n that make denominators zero; verify target_evaluation_point is not in known_points unless problem intends a removable singularity case.

instance_acceptance_rules: compute q(x) = auxiliary_factor·p(x) - (appropriate polynomial in x from rearranging given values) and ensure q(x) factors as (linear_factor)·P(x) with consistent linear_factor degree; verify arithmetic (P(target), q(target), p(target)) and reduce final fraction to lowest terms.

distractor_guidance: produce distractors reflecting common mistakes: using P(target) off by a factor, sign errors in q(target), failing to reduce fraction, or swapping numerator/denominator in intermediate steps.

novelty_guidance: prefer structural variations (different auxiliary_factor, different formula family, different degree) over trivial numeric substitutions to keep reasoning pattern but create new algebraic work.

validation_examples: derive P(target) explicitly and compute q at special points (roots of auxiliary_factor) to solve for linear_factor before evaluating at target; check that final answer matches one of the rendered choices exactly in MathML.
fallback_generation_hint: If structural generation fails, produce an instance by shifting the consecutive block by +1 (start at 3), keep degree_of_p = 5, use value_formula n/(n^2 - 1) and auxiliary_factor x^2 - 1, and set target = start + count (e.g., ask for p(9)). This preserves solvability and keeps novelty while ensuring arithmetic stays manageable.
